I'm planning implementation of Story 4.2 "Per-Entry Sync Badge" in a Flutter app (Cerne, Clean Architecture, flutter_bloc, fpdart Either). I need a distilled investigation report (not a dump of full file contents) covering exactly the following, each with precise file path + line numbers / symbol names so I can build a "Code Map" for a spec document. Repo root: /Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b

Context: Story 4.1 (chronological entry list) just shipped. It added `EntriesRepository.list()`, `Entry` entity, `MeusRegistrosCubit`, `EntryRecordCard` widget (no tap handler currently), Hive-backed offline fallback. Story 4.2 must add:
1. A single pure-Dart derivation function in `entries/domain` that computes a sync badge state (Synchronizing / Synchronization error / Synchronized) from `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, plus "transient per-entry write state" (in-flight / failed write tracking that doesn't exist yet — I need to know what write-tracking state currently exists, if any, after a `create()` call).
2. A badge UI component (dot + accessible label, retry tap target ≥44pt) rendered on `EntryRecordCard`.
3. Tap-to-retry on the error state: re-invoke the same underlying failed write (there's no separate retry endpoint) — but only when the underlying Failure is "retryable"; otherwise show inline explanation. I need to know if there's already any "retryable" classification/taxonomy for `Failure` types in this codebase or in `docs/input/backend/` (error taxonomy docs), and exactly which Failure variants exist today (`lib/core/failure/failure.dart`).
4. The badge's update stream must be "fully independent of the auth/session stream" and composed "only through the domain layer — no BLoC/Cubit ever references another BLoC/Cubit directly" (AD-7). I need to find: how does the app currently expose "auth status" as a stream/service (e.g. an AuthCubit, a session state stream, token refresh listener)? Where is `ExpiryOverlayHost` defined and how does it currently get its auth-expiry signal — does any existing feature already combine two streams only via the domain layer (a precedent pattern to mirror), or would this be the first?
5. Where/how is `Entry.serverRevision` and `Entry.updatedAt` currently defined on the `Entry` entity (exact fields, types, nullability) — `lib/features/entries/domain/entities/entry.dart`.
6. Where does the entries `create()` write call currently live end-to-end (cubit/state/repository/datasource) that a capture flow (text/audio/photo) invokes — I need the call chain so I know where "write in flight" / "write failed" state would need to be tracked and surfaced back up to whatever cubit renders the record card list (`MeusRegistrosCubit` in `entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_cubit.dart`). Is there already any notion of a locally-created-but-not-yet-confirmed Entry, or does `create()` block until the server responds (i.e., is there actually anything to be "Synchronizing" about per entry, or does this only matter for a retry-after-failure case)?
7. Design tokens available for green/ochre/red dot colors — check `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` for existing named colors matching sync states (don't invent new ones; report exact token names only).
8. Existing shared value-equality / sealed-state patterns used in this codebase (the pattern `MeusRegistrosState` and `EntriesPage`/`EntryDateGroup` follow) so a new value class for badge state matches existing conventions — just name the pattern, point to one example file, don't re-explain it.
9. Tap target sizing convention already used elsewhere (≥44pt) — is there an existing constant/token for minimum tap target size, or was 44pt literal until now?

Report back as a concise structured list (file:line for every claim), organized by the 9 numbered points above. Do not include large code excerpts — just the facts I need (signatures, field names, exact existing patterns) plus 1-2 line snippets only where genuinely necessary to settle an ambiguity. Keep total response under 600 words.

tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

## 4. Auth/session stream + AD-7 precedent
- Auth status stream: `SessionRepository.statusStream` → `Stream<SessionStatus>`, `lib/features/auth/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart:16`. `SessionStatus` enum (`authenticated, unauthenticated, expired`) at `lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart:13`.

- `ExpiryOverlayHost` — `lib/core/navigation/expiry_overlay_host.dart:35-51` (StatefulWidget, constructor takes `sessionRepository`, `router`, `navigatorKey`, `child`); subscribes directly to `sessionRepository.statusStream` via a single `StreamSubscription<SessionStatus>` (`_subscription` field, line 54) in its State — it is a **widget**, not a Cubit, and only consumes **one** stream.
- AD-7 precedent check: no existing file combines two domain streams. `grep` for `StreamGroup|rxdart|CombineLatestStream` across `lib/` and `pubspec.yaml` returns nothing — **no rxdart dependency, no precedent pattern**. Story 4.2 would be the first case of combining two independent domain streams; `AuthCubit` doc (`lib/features/auth/presentation/cubit/auth_cubit.dart:15-19`) is the clearest existing articulation of AD-7 itself ("a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit... never a BLoC-to-BLoC reference (AD-7)") but gives no multi-stream-composition example to mirror.

## 5. `Entry.serverRevision`/`updatedAt` fields
`lib/features/entries/domain/entities/entry.dart:24-51` — plain class (no freezed, mirrors `AuthenticatedUser`). Relevant fields: `final int serverRevision` (line 45), `final String updatedAt` (line 47, kept as raw ISO-8601 string, not parsed — per class doc lines 18-23). Both non-nullable. Comment explicitly forbids adding fields beyond the exact documented set (lines 11-13).

## 6. `create()` call chain — blocking, no pending-write state today
Callers: `lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/text_entry_cubit.dart:126`, `.../audio_entry_cubit.dart:530`, `.../photo_entry_cubit.dart:360` → all call `EntriesRepository.create()` (interface `lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart:18-22`) → impl `lib/features/entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart:36` → `EntriesRemoteDataSource`.

The only meaningful "Synchronizing/error" state 4.2 could show today is for a *new* retry mechanism that doesn't exist yet — this is new ground, not a wire-up of existing plumbing.
